neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case is that the accused, who were neighbors, had a land dispute with the victim. On the day of the incident, the victim was repairing his wall when the accused approached him, leading to an altercation. The accused, armed with firearms and other weapons, fired upon the victim, causing injuries to his left foot and right arm. The victim was taken to a clinic where medical evidence confirmed that the injuries were caused by firearms. Witnesses testified that the accused were present at the scene with weapons and that the victim sustained injuries as a result of the altercation. The medical evidence corroborated that the injuries were caused by firearms, and the prosecution argued that the accused used the weapons due to the ongoing dispute.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellants were present at the place of occurrence armed with guns and caused injury to the informant. The medical evidence corroborated that the injuries were caused by firearms, and the testimony of witnesses established the use of firearms in the altercation. The prosecution also highlighted the previous enmity between the parties due to a land dispute.

quotes.text: The prosecution case in brief is as under: On the basis of fardbeyan of PW-6 (injured informant), Kumar Nandan Singh made at the clinic of Dr. Himkar, the police registered an FIR being Case No. 312 of 1999 dated 10.10.1999, Police Station - Lakhi Sarai, under Sections 323, 307 read with Section 34 IPC and Section 27 of the Arms Act.
The medical evidence adduced by the prosecution has great corroborative value as it proves that the injuries could have been caused in the manner alleged.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution's story was doubtful due to the delayed submission of the FIR and contradictions in the testimony of prosecution witnesses. They also claimed that there was no material to indicate recovery of any gun or bullet, and that the presence of the accused at the scene was questionable due to the alibi plea.

quotes.text: Mrs. Anjana Prakash, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants vehemently submitted that though the conviction is under Section 27 of the Arms Act but there is no material available on record to indicate recovery of any gun or any seizure memo showing recovery of any bullet or pellets from the spot.

She also points out that even though the fardbeyan was recorded on 10.10.1999 and First Information Report was registered on the same day but the same was sent to the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate on 12.10.1999 and in the absence of any explanation for delayed submission of FIR, the whole prosecution story becomes doubtful.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that minor contradictions in witness testimony cannot discredit the testimony, and that medical evidence is crucial to corroborate the prosecution's case. The court also emphasized that the use of firearms in causing injury under Section 324 IPC is punishable, and that the use of arms is governed by Section 27 of the Arms Act.

quotes.text: The testimony of a witness in a criminal trial cannot be discarded merely because of minor contradictions or omission as observed by this court in Narayan Chetanram Chaudhary & Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra 1.

The evidentiary value of a medical witness is very crucial to corroborate the case of prosecution and it is not merely a check upon testimony of eyewitnesses, it is also independent testimony, because it may establish certain facts, quite apart from the other oral evidence.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the charge under Section 324 IPC was established against the appellants, and they could not escape the punishment for using arms prescribed by Section 27 of the Arms Act.

quotes.text: Once the charge against the appellants under Section 324 IPC of voluntarily causing injuries by firearm, which is a dangerous weapon stands established, they cannot escape the punishment for using arms prescribed by Section 27 of the Arms Act.
